headline: Ideas to cut costs and raise revenue were presented, including parking fees, health insurance, and payments from tax-exempt institutions; no votes were taken.
summary: The meeting presented early research on ways to reduce the city's deficit and raise revenue. Ideas included health insurance, pensions, parking fees, enterprise funds, and state school aid. No votes were taken, and a list of recommendations is planned for spring 2027.
discussion: Parking fees on Lothrop Street: Speakers asked that any fee increase be phased in gradually to protect downtown businesses, and that the beach-area parking zone not charge residents.
Health insurance costs: Healthcare was described as the biggest driver of the deficit, with double-digit increases for the city each year over the last four years.
Structural deficit causes: One speaker said staff salaries and benefits are the main issue, and that the city must decide its values and what it can pay for.
Tax-exempt institution payments: The 25 percent Boston benchmark was discussed, with the average receipt described as 3 to 7 percent, so cash payments were not expected to be large.
Chapter 70 school funding: Beverly was described as funding about 30 percent over its foundation budget, and a one-time state payout of about $118 per student was noted as stuck in committee.
